clue.text: Right season to produce young

parts.note: in cricket the off side is the right-hand side of the field for a right-handed batsman, so right gives off
spring is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: Farming advice that the correct time of year is the moment to raise young animals.
explanation.walkthrough: OFF for 'right' is a cricket term: the off side is the right-hand half of the field for a right-handed batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a parent's children, the young it produces.

clue.text: Be exceedingly good, and escape belt

parts.note: out is an exit or way of escape
a belt of land is a strip

explanation.surface: Someone excellent who also gets away from a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to surpass or exceed others, i.e. to excel.

clue.text: E.g. bird's small bill

definitions.meaning: a bird is an example of a creature that flies
a handbill or leaflet advertising something

explanation.surface: A bird's tiny beak, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that flies, such as a bird, is one; it is also a small printed advertisement handed out.

clue.text: Show amount of time spent in store

indicators.note: spent in says the time piece goes inside the store

parts.note: a pantry is a store room for food
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A report on how long was spent in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb but is the noun definition; 'spent in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is elaborate ceremonial display, i.e. a grand show.

clue.text: Fumes with anger

definitions.meaning: sweet-smelling smoke from burning resin or sticks
as a verb, to make someone furious

explanation.surface: Someone seething with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is fragrant smoke, and the verb with the stress on the second syllable means to enrage.

clue.text: Animated girl given celebration meal

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A lively young woman treated to a festive dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated' means brought to life: in Greek myth Pygmalion's statue, later named GALATEA, was given life.
explanation.definitionFit: In the myth a sculptor's ivory statue of a woman was brought to life, literally animated.

clue.text: Notes problem about one chapter

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for the problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A student's notes describe a problem relating to one chapter of a textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SUM to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is written as notes on a stave, so notes stands for the art itself.

clue.text: Doctor has to treat someone retiring

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
to use someone is to treat them, especially badly

explanation.surface: A GP must care for a patient who is going into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests leaving work; it means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A timid, shy person is figuratively a small rodent that hides away.

clue.text: Ordinary female in smart clothing — creature with formidable weapon

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for smart dress

parts.note: swish means fashionable and smart, of clothing or style
ORD is an abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A plain woman in elegant dress, then a fearsome armed beast.
explanation.definitionFit: This large ocean fish has a long sword-like upper jaw used as a weapon.

clue.text: Yarn that sounds bloodthirsty

indicators.note: that sounds says we want a word pronounced like the following one

parts.note: cruel means savage, delighting in suffering

explanation.surface: A tale that seems savage in nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' tempts as a story; it is wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a thin worsted wool thread used for embroidery.

clue.text: Object initially to his impractical new gadget

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone objects at the outset to a relative's useless new contraption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a verb ('object to'), but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object, an item not otherwise named.

clue.text: Paint you reportedly waste on a small room

indicators.note: on means the following pieces are placed onto the earlier piece, after it in the answer

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison

indicators.note: reportedly says a word is to be taken by how it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced the same as the word you
to lose time is to waste it

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone squanders paint decorating a tiny room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' applies only to 'you', giving a single letter; 'on' means the later pieces sit after the room's word, and 'Paint' is the definition, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose paint is a lacquer based on cellulose, used on cars, so the name of the material stands for the coating.

clue.text: Land in which turtle has no pressure

indicators.note: has no means the following letter is to be dropped from the word for the turtle

parts.note: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A country where a turtle lives free of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes P from TERRAPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of ground judged by its physical features, i.e. land.

clue.text: Downtrodden control freak altered

indicators.note: freak, as a verb meaning to streak or mottle oddly, says the following word's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A freak who wants to control everything has changed, now crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'control freak' looks like one phrase; split it: 'control' ends the definition and 'freak' signals the anagram of ALTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot pedal that drives a machine, a control literally pressed down by the foot.

clue.text: Successful negotiators enter thus, as well

definitions.meaning: people who have struck a deal have entered into an agreement, read literally as going in to the deal
an idiom meaning in addition, besides

explanation.surface: A remark about how winning dealmakers come in, and what they get besides.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in addition, and literally describes entering an agreement once negotiation succeeds.

clue.text: Rival club said to avoid bad luck

parts.note: to touch is to rival, as in 'nobody can touch her'
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A competitor's club spoken of as a charm against misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is uttered, like 'knock on wood', to ward off misfortune after tempting fate.

clue.text: Suffer from two rude and violent people

parts.note: a Goth, from the Germanic tribe, is an uncivilised barbarian
rough as a noun means thugs, ruffians

explanation.surface: Being harmed by a pair of boorish thugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'people' are a GOTH (a barbarian) and a ROUGH (a ruffian).
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something is to endure or undergo it.

clue.text: Many turned up with no liking for work, showing little emotion

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lots means many
idly means lazily, without working

explanation.surface: A crowd arrived reluctant to work and seemed quite unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses LOTS to STOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive, so acting this way is without visible feeling.

clue.text: Butchery that he needed to change to bring peace

indicators.note: to change says the letters of the preceding words must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gruesome act that someone had to change in order to make peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges BUTCHERY, THAT and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the custom of interring weapons when warring sides made a treaty, so it means end a quarrel.

clue.text: With end of war, is home provided in exchange for this?

definitions.text: With end of war, is home provided in exchange for this?

indicators.note: in exchange says the letters are swapped around into a new order
end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A soldier wonders whether, when the war ends, a home is the reward for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of war' gives R; 'in exchange' rearranges R, IS and HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is great bravery, the kind a nation might reward with a home after the fighting.

clue.text: Home somewhat confined in Derby, say

indicators.note: confined in says the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat, so an example of a hat
a bit means somewhat, slightly

explanation.surface: A house that is a little cramped in the city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the English city; with 'say' it is an example of a HAT (a bowler).
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where a plant or animal lives.

clue.text: Reptile's head

definitions.meaning: a headland; the peninsula at Britain's southernmost point in Cornwall

explanation.surface: The head of a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' means headland: the Lizard is a Cornish peninsula, mainland Britain's most southerly point.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a scaly reptile and the name of a famous promontory in Cornwall.

clue.text: Asthmatic uses this at home, getting healthier

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in tonight'
hale means healthy, so haler is healthier

explanation.surface: An asthma sufferer feels better using medicine at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An asthma patient breathes medicine from a small spray device to open the airways.

clue.text: Crazy year after game is over

indicators.note: after says the year letter follows the reversed game
is over means turned over, so the game's name is read backwards

parts.note: pool is a game played with cues on a table

explanation.surface: A mad twelve months follow the end of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' reverses POOL to LOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Last resort after boy turned the wrong way?

definitions.text: Last resort after boy turned the wrong way?

indicators.note: after says the scrambled letters come behind the reversed name
turned the wrong way says the boy's name is read backwards

parts.note: Rob is a boy's name

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, says the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reform school as the final resort for a lad who went off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned the wrong way' reverses ROB to BOR; 're-sort' rearranges LAST to STAL. A BORSTAL was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's institutions for young offenders were the place a delinquent lad was sent when all else failed.

clue.text: Juvenile Italian upset, affected by the moon

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A young Italian distressed and swayed by the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAD IT into TI DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean tides are caused by the moon's gravity, so this describes anything governed by the moon's pull.

clue.text: Restricting sport's unfair to elderly champion

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: agist is a variant spelling of ageist, prejudiced against older people
polo is a sport played on horseback; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A complaint that limiting a sport is unjust to a veteran title-holder.
explanation.walkthrough: The unfairness word uses the less common spelling without its middle E. 'champion' is not a title-winner but someone who argues for a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist defends or argues for a cause or person, so is a supporter or advocate.

clue.text: Sound idea to some extent brought to nothing

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sensible plan that came partly to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to reverse it, cancelling its effect entirely.

clue.text: Father protecting daughters in revolutionary period

indicators.note: protecting means guarding all round, so the period's word surrounds the daughters

parts.note: a day is the time the earth takes for one revolution on its axis
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A father shielding his girls during a time of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics, but means one turn of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy is a child's familiar word for a father.

clue.text: In which clubmen compete to provide equally dramatic spectacle

parts.note: to match is to equal, supplying something of the same standard
a play is a drama performed on stage

explanation.surface: Seeking an equally theatrical show where club members compete.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'clubmen' are golfers: in this format each hole is won or lost, rather than counting total strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers with clubs play a format scored hole by hole against an opponent.
